reason: The caller-owned BlobServiceClient factory validates inputs and passes its container client into the repository without taking ownership of the client.
The selector creates a BlobServiceClient from the supplied connection string and returns one Azure Blob repository; input and default container boundaries are explicit.

SAS-free claim-check addresses, current-client retrieval of legacy signed addresses, caller stream handling, and MaxValue unbounded metadata were reviewed; explicit TTL currently writes only ValidUntilUtc metadata and does not enforce expiry or reclaim an unaccessed blob.
Compressed uploads stage bounded blocks and commit with a no-overwrite condition; a per-attempt random prefix now prevents block-ID reuse when concurrent uploads collide on the same blob name.
The extension contract requires a nonempty unique blob name, and the repository rejects empty names before transport use.
The default generator uses new sequential IDs with the established compact formatter; the unit test checks nonempty distinct consecutive outputs.
The lock records Azure.Storage.Blobs 12.29.2 as the direct dependency with Azure.Core and Azure.Storage.Common transitive dependencies; the project reference and graph were read.
